goldman.text: Vālmīki, the ascetic, questioned the eloquent Nārada, bull among sages, always devoted to asceticism and study of the sacred texts.

iast: ko nv asmin sāmprataṃ loke guṇavān kaś ca vīryavān
dharmajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca satyavākyo dṛḍhavrataḥ

goldman.text: “Is there a man in the world today who is truly virtuous? Who is there who is mighty and yet knows both what is right and how to act upon it? Who always speaks the truth and holds firmly to his vows?

iast: cāritreṇa ca ko yuktaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ko hitaḥ
vidvān kaḥ kaḥ samarthaś ca kaś caikapriyadarśanaḥ
dev: चारित्रेण च को युक्तः सर्वभूतेषु को हितः ।

goldman.text: Who exemplifies proper conduct and is benevolent to all creatures? Who is learned, capable, and a pleasure to behold?

iast: kasya bibhyati devāś ca jātaroṣasya saṃyuge

goldman.text: Who is self-controlled, having subdued his anger? Who is both judicious and free from envy? Who, when his fury is aroused in battle, is feared even by the gods?

iast: etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
maharṣe tvaṃ samartho 'si jñātum evaṃvidhaṃ naram
dev: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे ।

goldman.text: This is what I want to hear, for my desire to know is very strong. Great seer, you must know of such a man.”

iast: śrutvā caitat trilokajño vālmīker nārado vacaḥ
śrūyatām iti cāmantrya prahṛṣṭo vākyam abravīt

goldman.text: When Nārada, who was familiar with all the three worlds, heard Vālmīki’s words, he was delighted. “Listen,” he replied and spoke these words:

iast: bahavo durlabhāś caiva ye tvayā kīrtitā guṇāḥ
mune vakṣyāmy ahaṃ buddhvā tair yuktaḥ śrūyatāṃ naraḥ
dev: बहवो दुर्लभाश्चैव ये त्वया कीर्तिता गुणाः ।
मुने वक्ष्याम्यहं बुद्ध्वा तैर्युक्तः श्रूयतां नरः ॥

goldman.text: “The many virtues you have named are hard to find. Let me think a moment, sage, before I speak. Hear now of a man who has them all.
His name is Rāma and he was born in the House of Ikṣvāku. All men know of him, for he is self-controlled, mighty, radiant, steadfast, and masterful.
He is wise and grounded in proper conduct. Eloquent and majestic, he annihilates his enemies. His shoulders are broad and his arms mighty. His neck is like a conch shell and his jaws are powerful.

His chest is vast, and a subduer of his enemies, he wields a huge bow. His collarbone is set deep in muscle, his arms reach down to his knees, and his head is finely made. His brow is noble and his gait full of grace.

His proportions are perfect and his limbs well formed and symmetrical. Dark is his complexion and he is valorous. His chest is fully fleshed; he has large eyes. He is splendid and marked with all auspicious signs.

iast: dharmajñaḥ satyasaṃdhaś ca prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ
dev: धर्मज्ञः सत्यसंधश्च प्रजानां च हिते रतः ।

goldman.text: “He knows the ways of righteousness and is always true to his word. The welfare of his subjects is his constant concern. He is renowned, learned, pure, disciplined, and contemplative.
He is the protector of all living things and the guardian of righteousness. Versed in the essence of the vedas and their ancillary sciences, he is expert in the science of arms.
He is versed in the essence of every śāstra, learned in traditional lore, and highly intelligent. All the people love him, for he is good, cheerful, and clever.
He is the constant resort of good men, as is the ocean of rivers. For he is noble and equable in all circumstances and always a pleasure to behold.

iast: samudra iva gāmbhīrye dhairyeṇa himavān iva

goldman.text: “The delight of his mother, Kausalyā, he is gifted with every virtue. For he is as deep as the ocean and as unyielding as the Himalayas.
He is as mighty as Viṣṇu, but as pleasant to behold as the moon. In his wrath he resembles the fire at the end of time, yet he rivals the earth in forbearance.

iast: dhanadena samas tyāge satye dharma ivāparaḥ

goldman.text: In charity he is the equal of Kubera, giver of wealth, and in truthfulness like a second Dharma, the god of righteousness.
goldman.note: Goldman carries 1.1.18b (tam evaṃguṇasaṃpannaṃ rāmaṃ satyaparākramam) into the next sentence, shown under 1.1.19.

iast: jyeṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhaguṇair yuktaṃ priyaṃ daśarathaḥ sutam

goldman.text: Moved by affection for him, Daśaratha, lord of the earth, wished to appoint this Rāma, his beloved eldest son, as prince regent. For he was truly valorous, possessed all these virtues, and was gifted with other excellent virtues.
goldman.note: This sentence renders 1.1.18b and 1.1.19 together, in Goldman's order.

goldman.source: Robert P. Goldman et al., trans., The Rāmāyaṇa of Vālmīki: The Complete English Translation, revised and edited by Robert P. Goldman and Sally J. Sutherland Goldman (Princeton: Princeton University Press, 2021). Bālakāṇḍa translated by Robert P. Goldman.
